newsitem.title: UK: World oil price to stay weak until 2000-2010 - CGE.
newsitem.headline: World oil price to stay weak until 2000-2010 - CGE.

text.p: World oil prices will remain weak for the rest of the decade as rising supply continues to outpace demand growth, according to a new study by the Centre For Global Energy Studies (CGES) published on Wednesday.

Assuming a substantial increase in production capacity within the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), continuing growth in non-OPEC output until the year 2001 and the full lifting of sanctions against Iraq from 1999 onwards, CGES expects prices to decline from the 1996 peak for four or five years.
"It seems that non-OPEC output holds the key to future oil prices, for when it it stops growing we find that real oil prices start to rise," the CGES said.
The key feature of the reference case scenario is a weakening of the oil price in nominal terms between now and the years 2000-1, it said.

Despite an increase in global oil demand of 6.9 million barrels per day (bpd) over the period 1996-2000 the price of oil will weaken in money-of-the-day terms to around $15 a barrel where it will stay until the year 2002.
The report said the price weakness was because potential supply would rise by more than the 6.9 million bpd jump in demand.

Non-OPEC output is expected to rise by 3.4 million bpd between 1996 and 2001 while Iraq should be producing at capacity from 1999 onwards, which would bring another 2.5 million bpd into play within two years.
